text:
maria: Quick postmortem follow-up: we need to convert the incident findings into concrete action items for GPU capacity and autoscale. Please claim a task and drop an ETA (date) in this thread by EOD today so I can add to the tracker.

devon: I can take scheduler tuning (bin-packing rules, preemption thresholds, max-pods-per-gpu). Planning a small canary in prod with traffic shaping. ETA: 2026-04-02 EOD.

aj: Ill own headroom policy + autoscaler behavior changes (stabilization/cooldown and scale rate). Need to gather tail-latency traces first to set safe numbers. ETA: proposal 2026-03-30 EOD.

kim: Cloud quota ticket opened (CS-2026-5512). Support asked for 1hr peak profile; gave them current fleet + 40% as a starting ask. Expecting reply within 48h. Will post updates. If quota request stalls, fallback: cross-region spill or smaller model autoswitch.

oliver: Ill draft an "oncall playbook" for GPU pressure events (checks, quick fixes, comms templates). First draft 2026-03-28.

sre-bot: Incident snapshot: GPU pool saturated at 2026-03-18 14:03 PDT. Autoscaler slow due to long node provisioning and conservative scaleUp policy. Logs: /infra/logs/2026-03-18/gpu-scale-events.log

devex: Ill add the missing telemetry: per-model token-rate, per-pod GPU mem util, and autoscaler decision traces. Dashboard panels + alerts in a PR. ETA: 2026-03-31 EOD.

aj: Draft autoscaler behavior snippet (will iterate in PR):
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
spec:
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 20
      policies:
        - type: Percent
          value: 250
          periodSeconds: 60
    scaleDown:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 240
      policies:
        - type: Percent
          value: 50
          periodSeconds: 60
```
Initial headroom: reserve 20% of GPUs for bursty chat; we can tune down after a 2-week canary.

maria: Noted: recurring pattern seems to be the daily batch finisher + partner jobs around 14:00 PDT. Two mitigation paths: 1) shift heavy non-critical batches to late-night windows, 2) keep a small hot pool + fast scale-up policy.

kim: Cloud team wants explicit burst numbers (peak concurrent pods, expected ramp time). @devon @aj can you attach estimates? I put a conservative ramp of 15 minutes in the ticket for now.

devon: Will run a short load profile to estimate 1hr peak GPU/pod counts and post by 2026-03-26 noon.

oliver: Playbook quick checklist (initial):
- Check capacity dashboard + top consuming namespaces
- If GPU avg util > 80% for 10m -> escalate and increase reserved headroom
- If autoscaler unable to add nodes -> open quota escalation and route non-critical traffic to smaller model variants
- If node provisioning latency > 5m -> consider warm pool + pre-provision policy
Ill add exact kubectl / cloud commands and links.

maria: Ill consolidate these into the postmortem action-tracker and set weekly checkpoints (Wednesdays) until items closed. If owners need more runway, ping me. :white_check_mark:

aj: Confirmed: headroom policy PR by 2026-03-30 EOD.

devon: Confirmed: scheduler canary + perf numbers by 2026-04-02 EOD.

kim: Updating CS-2026-5512 in this thread; next cloud update expected 2026-03-24.

devex: Instrumentation PR ETA: 2026-03-31 EOD, will include alerts for hot shards and autoscaler failures.

maria: Thanks all. Ill create the tracker rows and assign. Adding a weekly reminder on Wednesdays for 6 weeks. If anything slips, report new ETA here. :thumbsup:
